transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. 

Well, I suppose what brings me in is that my wife thinks I'm not eating enough. But honestly, most days I just have my coffee and a piece of toast in the morning, and then maybe some soup or a few vegetables later on in the day. I just find that big meals feel pretty unnecessary at my age.
Do you avoid these larger meals because you are worried about gaining weight or because you are unhappy with your body shape?

Well, yes, I suppose it is about the weight. When my wife tries to put butter on things, or if she serves me a full plate, I just get nervous. I worry that I'll start putting weight back on, and... well, I just don't want to lose the control I've worked so hard to keep.
Could you tell me how much you currently weigh and how tall you are?

I'm about five foot nine, and right now I weigh around 125 pounds. My regular doctor told me that number has gotten too low, but... I don't really see it that way. Being a bit lighter just makes it easier on my joints, you know? It helps me get around the garden and keep up with my daily walks without feeling weighed down.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you feel like your current weight is appropriate, or do you see yourself as being heavier than what the scale says?

Well, I wouldn't say I see myself as heavy, exactly. It's more about... how things fit and look. Like, if my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. It means I'm keeping things in check. But if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, even just a little, I feel... well, sloppy. I just get really disappointed in myself. I want to look trim, not soft.
Have you noticed any physical changes lately, such as feeling unusually cold all the time, losing hair, or experiencing fatigue?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I get a little tired sometimes after working in the yard, but I'm 78, so that's just part of getting older, I figure. And my hair's been thinning for years anyway. But no, I don't feel unusually cold or wiped out. Physically, I feel pretty normal.
Have you noticed a significant decrease in your interest in sexual activity since your weight has dropped?

No, I can't really say that I have. I mean, at my age, that sort of thing has naturally slowed down over the years anyway. I haven't noticed any sudden drop-off or change recently just because my weight went down. It's just been about the same as it has been for a good while now.

Do you ever find yourself eating a large amount of food in a short period of time, or do you ever feel the need to exercise excessively or use other methods, like vomiting or laxatives, to compensate after eating?

No, I don't do anything like that. I don't eat big amounts of food all at once, and I definitely don't make myself sick or take laxatives. I just... I just eat my regular meals, just smaller portions, and I keep active around the house and the yard. That's about it.
Do you feel that your fear of gaining weight is so intense that it significantly interferes with your ability to enjoy social activities or your daily routine?

I wouldn't say it's my fear that gets in the way, exactly. I still keep up with most of my chores around the house just fine. But, well... my wife has started cutting our outings short lately. Or she'll insist I sit out of the community tours we usually do, just because she worries I haven't eaten enough to keep my strength up. So I guess it does interfere a bit with our social things, mostly because she gets so concerned about it.
When you are at your lowest weight, do you still feel that certain parts of your body, like your stomach or hips, look too large?

Well, yes. I mostly just pay attention to my midsection. If my belt feels a notch looser, I feel like I've done right by myself. But... if I look in the mirror and my stomach looks the least bit rounded, I just feel sloppy. And disappointed. So, I guess I do still focus on that, yeah.
When your primary care doctor told you that your weight of 125 pounds was too low, did you believe them, or did you feel that they were mistaken about your physical health?

Honestly, I think he was mistaken. I just... I don't really see why everyone is making such a big fuss about my weight. Older folks are supposed to eat less as they age, anyway. It's a natural thing. And like I said, I'm still managing my chores around the house just fine, and I can still do those community tours. So, no, I didn't really believe him. I think my health is perfectly fine.
Have you noticed any changes in your sexual desire or performance that you might attribute to your current weight?

Well, no, not really. I mean... at my age, that's just not something my wife and I focus on much anymore anyway. So, no, I haven't noticed any changes like that, and I definitely wouldn't say my weight has had anything to do with it.
Are you currently taking any medications for any health conditions, or have you been diagnosed with any medical issues that might affect your appetite or how you process food?
No, I'm not taking any medications like that. I don't have any medical conditions that affect my appetite or digestion or anything. Like I said, I think I'm perfectly healthy.
